q: The government agency responsible for organizing national elections in Nigeria is ____. (P5)
explain: The Independent National Electoral Commission conducts presidential, governorship, and legislative elections.

q: The system of government where power belongs to the people through elected representatives is ____. (P5)
explain: Democracy is government of the people, by the people, and for the people.

q: The principle that everyone, including leaders, must obey the law equally is the ____. (P5)
explain: The Rule of Law ensures justice, equality before law, and supremacy of the constitution.

q: The agency established to fight financial crimes and corruption in Nigeria is the ____. (P5)
explain: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission investigates graft and fraudulent practices.

q: The minimum voting age for a Nigerian citizen in national elections is ____ years. (P5)
explain: Section 117 of the Nigerian Constitution sets the franchise voting age at 18.

q: Civic duty (P5): Paying taxes promptly to the government is a civic ____.
explain: duty / obligation is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): Protecting public utilities like streetlights and water pipes is the responsibility of ____.
explain: all citizens is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): A citizen should always obey lawful orders from the ____.
explain: police and courts is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): Treating people of different ethnic groups and religions with kindness is called ____.
explain: tolerance and unity is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): Which of these is a civic responsibility of a student in school?
explain: Keeping the school compound clean is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): A child's right to life, healthcare, and education is protected by the ____ Act.
explain: Child Rights is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): When singing the National Anthem, citizens should ____.
explain: stand upright and pay attention is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): The Independent Corrupt Practices Commission is abbreviated as ____.
explain: ICPC is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): Refusing to join secret cults and violence in school demonstrates moral ____.
explain: courage and discipline is the essential civic principle.

q: Civic duty (P5): The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) was established in 1973 to promote national ____.
explain: unity and integration is the essential civic principle.
